title: Savoy Sultans, Lionel Hampton and a 1948 Pittsburgh show
summary: Memories of the Savoy Sultans, Rudy Powell and Ralph Cooper's broadcasts.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Right. In 1948, I believe it was they had 'A Night of Stars' in Pittsburgh and they had Lois Deppe with whom Earl Hines used to play and then they had Billy Eckstine and Errol Garner. They had four generations going for them. Earl had just become popular. Errol Garner. (Deletion)

Well, getting back to the Savoy Sultans with Panama Frances they made their debut down at Highlights in Jazz with Jack Klein singer (phonetic spelling) and I hadn't heard a band for so long and they sounded so good, of course they had nine pieces and you were saying that they didn't have some of the original --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, I think they had nine pieces when I saw them.
But it sounded good.
Very good.
And they're doing very good now.
And Hamp was out of sight.
Who's the alto player you're talking about -- way before, you said with the club foot.
No, the guy with the club foot, the tenor man was Rudy Powell.
Okay, he wasn't with the Savoy Sultans?
No, no.
Who am I confusing him with?

I'll never forget -- do you remember when Ralph Cooper was the Master of Ceremonies for a broadcast of the Kraft Cheese Company and they had Lionel Hampton and he went off playing, 'Flying Home' with the great Arnett Cobb.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yeah.
You know, Arnet, he's partially paralyzed.
Yeah, I know.
And he plays gigs, but he stays nearby where he lives. He doesn't travel too much.
He was playing in the West End, I believe.
